endorsements.quote: What is missing is the bridge – a clinical constitution for AI, developed in collaboration with the professions whose standards it would draw on, and informed by deliberative processes involving people with lived experience whom it ultimately seeks to benefit, to guide model training (Level 2) and oversight (Level 3).

Just as human clinical supervision facilitates longitudinal tracking of patient trajectories, LLM oversight must do the same, and it must include clear escalation pathways and mechanisms for adverse event reporting where even subtle harms are detected.
Detecting these longer-term patterns will require a substantial shift in how oversight is conceptualised and conducted.

unlisted_practices: Specify explicit, clinically grounded values for health AI through a clinical constitution that encodes a defensible range of therapeutic stances and is culturally appropriate to the populations served.
Curate pre-training data deliberately using clinically informed corpora and actively de-bias stigmatising or culturally narrow content.
Design post-training reward signals that value clinically appropriate friction alongside helpfulness, using clinician-informed annotation.
Measure alignment to the articulated values at each stage of model training.
Develop methods to evaluate longitudinal conversational trajectories across sessions to detect dependency, boundary erosion, and maladaptive reinforcement.
Define clearly the mechanisms for action when potential harm is detected in deployed AI.

Require developers of health AI to submit an alignment plausibility assurance case demonstrating that value specification, training, and oversight are consistent with safe outcomes, supported by pre- and post-deployment evidence.
Adopt alignment plausibility as a regulatory construct tied to the AI system or product for a defined health use, population, and deployment controls.
Invest in research on the measurement of alignment plausibility.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual and regulatory framework paper proposing 'alignment plausibility' as a standard for governing and assuring the safety of LLMs in healthcare (especially mental health).
